FERNANDEZ MARTINEZ AND MARTIN MEDICAL GROUP - DISCHARGE SUMMARY

Patient: Justin Sweeney
DOB: 03/14/2002
Sex: M
MRN: 640841

Admit: 09/09/2021
Discharge: 11/12/2025

Principal diagnosis: Eating disorder, recovered for approximately 7.8 years.
Secondary diagnosis: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD)

Hospital course:
Mr. Sweeney, a 23-year-old male, was admitted on September 9, 2021, primarily for management of his eating disorder and PTSD. During his hospitalization, he underwent a comprehensive evaluation including psychiatric assessments and nutritional counseling. His eating disorder, which had been diagnosed on September 9, 2021, has been well-managed and controlled, with no recent episodes reported. He has maintained a stable weight throughout his visits, with weights ranging from 126 to 140 pounds. blood pressure has also remained within normal limits, varying between 117/75 mmHg and 130/81 mmHg across visits.

Mr. has been compliant with his regimen, which includes prazosin 1 mg his PTSD. His PTSD symptoms have been controlled with this medication, and he reports no significant distress or impairment in daily functioning related to PTSD. During his stay, he participated in individual therapy sessions and group support meetings, which were beneficial in reinforcing his coping strategies and emotional regulation.

His hospital course was uneventful, and he was discharged home in stable condition on November 12, 2025. At the time of discharge, his vital signs were stable with a blood pressure of 130/81 mmHg and a weight of 134 pounds. Physical examination revealed no acute distress, and all systems were normal.

Discharge medications:
- Prazosin 1 mg daily for PTSD

Social history:
Mr. Sweeney reports approximately one alcoholic drink per week. He denies any tobacco use. Family history is significant for COPD in his father, who was diagnosed at age 74.

Follow-up:
Mr. Sweeney is scheduled for a follow-up appointment with Dr. Daniel Rivera, his attending psychiatrist, in four weeks to assess his mental health status and adherence to medication. He is encouraged to continue with his outpatient therapy and support groups. Additionally, he will have a routine physical examination scheduled with his primary care physician to monitor his overall health and weight.

In summary, Mr. Sweeney has shown significant improvement and stability in managing his eating disorder and PTSD. He is discharged with a plan for continued outpatient management and support.

Dear Colleague,

I saw Justin Sweeney in consultation on May 17, 2026. Mr. Sweeney was referred to me for ongoing management of his Factor V Leiden mutation, which has been complicated by venous thromboembolism (VTE) of the factor V Leiden type. Currently, the condition is controlled without the use of any medications.

During the consultation, I reviewed the patient's history and current status. Mr. Sweeney reports no new symptoms and has had no recent VTE events. On examination, his vital signs were stable with a blood pressure of 127/81 and a of 138 lbs. The physical exam was otherwise unremarkable with normal findings.

Regarding compliance, it is important to note that Mr. Sweeney has been non-compliant with scheduled follow-up appointments, having missed two appointments since his last visit. Additionally, he reports consuming approximately one alcoholic drink per week.

Social history reveals that Mr. Sweeney's father had COPD, which led to his death at the age of 74, although no specific age of onset is provided. Unfortunately, he is not a candidate for genetic testing at this time.

My impression is that Mr. Sweeney's Factor V Leiden mutation is currently well-managed without the need for anticoagulant therapy. However, his non-compliance with follow-up visits and potential risks associated with alcohol consumption warrant close monitoring.

I recommend continued regular monitoring for any signs of VTE, adherence to follow-up appointments, and consideration of lifestyle modifications to mitigate risk factors. It is crucial that Mr. Sweeney remains vigilant about his health and adheres to the recommended follow-up schedule to prevent potential complications.

Thank you for this referral. Please feel free to reach out
